title: Code research, first pass: editor and render details

facts.title: The Mission_03 burning barrel is the model Env_BarrelDrumFire, whose effect chunk uses the particle file Env_Fire_SM_Loop_01
facts.fact: mission_03.mgf lists the model Env_BarrelDrum_Fire.MGMODEL (sub-meshes embers, rubbish, barrel_farm, sign1). Its .mtb references SpecialEffects/Environment/Env_Fire_SM_Loop_01.mgparticle, whose emitters are fire 1-3, smoke (bd_smoke_sm.tif) and sparks. No MAEffect is placed on Mission_03, so the flame and dark smoke column come from the model's own effect chunk. The placed object that uses this model was not decoded.
facts.how_to_use: Open: which placed instance uses Env_BarrelDrumFire on Mission_03 (scene data not decoded). In-game trace or decoded object list needed.

facts.title: The game draws the Env_Highway_Light lightbulb mesh at night on Mission_01b, so the .mtb hide rule does not remove it at run time
facts.fact: On Mission_01b at night (IsNightTime=1, LightsOn=1) the running game draws the lightbulb mesh once per lamp: an opaque material_color_shift draw (texture Misc_168_LightPost, 81043000; 43 vertices; colour C0 255,255,228; writes alpha 0x34), which renders white. So the .mtb MAModSubObjectShow rule (Enable=0, EnableTree=1) does not hide the bulb in the running game under those flags. An Ill Wind 'post only' trace conflicts with this and is unexplained.
facts.how_to_use: Open: why the Ill Wind trace shows post only. Check LightsOn and LightsDisabled on that lamp (flag bits are in the wiki).

facts.title: On Mission_03 the sky is the sky_main alpha layer over a cleared black frame, with no opaque dome drawn
facts.fact: On Mission_03 the game draws the sky_main alpha layer over a cleared black frame; no opaque sky dome is drawn. The sample pixel at game 640,60 of 1280x960 reads 29,27,25.
facts.how_to_use: Open: single-pixel sample. Confirm on a second pixel before relying on it. The additive star layer (Sky_034_Stars) on the same map is a separate open question. Caveat: MCP/tracetools runs render at 640x480, so this reference pixel and any thin-detail reading may understate detail at a 3840x1600; confirm at that resolution.

facts.title: The Mission_04 pad floor draw uses two detail textures (808D1000 and 80E99000), both trilinear with no anisotropy, mixed by stage constant 7F7F7F7F
facts.fact: Game trace of the M04 pad floor (block draw 3104941, prog 00021, 3 stages, pixel 480,400 of the 640x480 frame): t0 = 808D1000 128x128 DXT1 (Details_010_cracked), t1 = 80E99000 256x256 DXT1 (Terrain MissionXX_Detail01.tif). Both have filter word 02062000 (min trilinear, mag linear, mip bias 0) and control0 4003FFC0 (aniso 1x, full mip chain 6/7, wrap). Stage constant C0 = 7F7F7F7F (0.5). UV of vertex 0: tex0 15.4844, tex1 1.49805. The colour map is not in this draw.

facts.title: A node_light lightmap min_color equals the ground-pool splat colour (M02 trace matches a retail point light exactly)
facts.fact: On M02 the traced ground-pool splat colour C0 = 557F7A69 equals the min_color 127, 122, 105 of the 255,245,211 point light in gocommando.mgf exactly. So the lightmap min_color of a node_light is the splat colour C0.rgb. Only one instance was compared, and min equals max in every retail lamp seen, so the lerp between min and max is untested.
facts.how_to_use: Open: test a lamp whose min_color differs from max_color before relying on the lerp.

facts.title: The Mission_01b pavement pixel is a MARoad complex road slab drawn in two passes (programs 0A624 and 08C21)
facts.fact: Pixel 150,320 of the Mission_01b frame is MARoad 131795, a complex road slab. Pass 1 (program 0A624: t0 PASSTHRU, t1 DOT_PRODUCT, t2 DOT_ST, t3 2D = 512 ground map 80A61000) gives R0 = ((2T0-1).(2V0-1)) x T3.a x C0 (sun 4E3F34) + T3.rgb, then x V1. Pass 2 (program 08C21: t2 CUBE, t3 = framebuffer) gives 2x(T3 x lerp(cube, base, base.a) + multi.g x (.18,18,1) + multi.b x (1,97,31)) + multi.r x T3.a x 0.698. Decoded with rcdec.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the sun constant and the ground-map sampling are from one pixel; check on a second road pixel.

facts.title: Three editor paths do not draw the Mission_04 pad floor: ground_mix final lerp, its tile uv scale and the stage-19 detail line
facts.fact: In the editor, forcing ground_mix final lerp to a constant 0.5, scaling the tile uv by 0.0484 (game uv ratio 10.3) in ground_mix and in the stage-19 line, all give bit-identical M04 pad-shot images. So none of these draws the pad floor. The editor pad shot shows detail0 x colour x light (mean 36,34,35) with colour-map alpha about 1 at the pad. The stage-19 detail1 tile alone is smeared streaks (mean 70,73,68), not the crisp game grid. The owner of the pad floor draw in the editor is unknown.
facts.how_to_use: Open: candidates are the layer-array path ginfo.x>1.5, or a different shader or dpar branch. Or trace a game prog-00021 floor on another map. Status: M04 floor OPEN.

facts.title: MAPointLight census of retail Mission_03 and Mission_01b: 18 of 21 M03 lights have LightMap=1 and all 5 M01b lights have LightMap=0
facts.fact: Editor dump of retail data. Mission_03: 18 of 21 MAPointLights have LightMap=1 (LightRadius 60-80 object reach, LightMapRadius 20 ground disc, LightMapColor equal to LightColor); 3 have LightMap=0. Mission_01b: 5 of 5 have LightMap=0 (LightRadius 5-10), one of them LightOn=0. Consistent with the existing pointlight-ground-splat fact. The alpha 0x60 ground disc in the game is not yet re-verified in-game.
facts.how_to_use: Open: in-game check of the alpha 0x60 disc on a LightMap=1 lamp (needs a g1 grant).

facts.title: tracetools.exe adds texstate, vertex-csv (with d0 columns) and ctxwrite trace flags; RECOMP_CAM_SET does not yet move the view
facts.fact: The tracetools build (the game source tree pkg, MechAssault 2 tracetools.exe) keeps the texdump4 flags and adds: RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE_TEXSTATE=1 (needs _PIXEL; prints texstate filter, ctl0, levels and uv per covering draw), RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE_VERTICES=prefix with RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE_TEXTURE=tex0 address (per-draw csv with d0r.d0a columns; x,y,z,w are screen-space oPos), and RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE_CTXWRITE=1 (also dumps constant-writing vertex programs). Verified on M04 and M09b (Env_Grass 80DC6000 gave 1056 files). RECOMP_CAM_SET moves the eye field but the 3D scene goes black, so the M05 pose is not yet unblocked.
facts.how_to_use: Superseded in part: the pose override (RECOMP_CAM_SET) now WORKS (verified 10-25 on M04, see recomp-cam-set-pose-override-works-m04-verified). The earlier 'scene goes black' statement is out of date. The texstate/vertex/ctxwrite flags stand.

facts.title: In-game A/B on a Mission_03 copy: MAPointLight LightMap=1 paints a bright ground disc plus object light; LightMap=0 gives object light only
facts.fact: In-game A/B on a Mission_03 copy with one authored MAPointLight. LightMap=1 gives a bright ground disc plus object light. LightMap=0 gives object light only. This confirms the ground disc is controlled by the LightMap flag.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the disc alpha 0x60 value is still unverified in-game (see the census fact).

facts.title: RECOMP_CAM_SET=ex,ey,ez,tx,ty,tz[,hfov] forces the human camera pose and the 3D world renders normally from it (M04 verified)
facts.fact: Forces the human camera pose each frame (ma2_cam_build_hook phase 0). The human view (camera+0x200) points at its builder via MEM32(view+0x154) (vtable 0045DDD0, = camera+0x390). The builder state S sits at builder+0x14 (S+0 eye, S+0x10 look vector, S+0x1C up, rows right/up/forward at S+0x28/0x38/0x48, w=0); the camera keeps a copy at camera+0x238. Writing S+0x88. (the derived block) caused the earlier black or garbled scenes, so the fix writes only S and the camera+0x238 copy. Test: eye 1085,70,950 -> 1105.022,37.836,902.622 hfov 60 shows the pad from higher up. Bisect flags: RECOMP_CAM_SET_NO238, RECOMP_CAM_SET_NOCAMFIELDS, RECOMP_CAM_SET_LEGACY (broken). Custom-scenario campaign levels (e.g. M05) have no camera object behind the human view, so [CAM-POSE] falls back to the newest view's builder.
facts.how_to_use: Gameplay pose starts at game time ~23-30 s; do not press Enter; the pose does not apply during cinemas.

facts.title: Mission_05 exact pose pair: editor water and foliage are darker than the game, far hills brighter, hex patch matches
facts.fact: Exact pose recovered in game: eye 1837.115,23.734,238.756, look -0.9647,-0.2249,0.1357, hfov 44 (editor arg 1837.1150,23.7340,238.7560,-0.9647,-0.2249,0.1357,39.20). The game side is the Mission_05_layers scenario (P4 layered copy), so ground may differ by the layers. Measured RGB means, game vs editor: water mid 101,97,103 vs 93,91,96; water right 101,100,104 vs 86,84,85 (editor 8-15% darker); foliage low-left 54,61,59 vs 42,47,29 (editor ~25% darker, yellow-green; game neutral/bluish); far hills 73,72,70 vs 82,81,79 (editor brighter at distance); hex patch 53,53,48 vs 55,55,47 (match). The game also shows ground mist over water and rippled water; the right-edge pylon is visible in the game but cut in the editor (FOV mapping: editor 39.20 for game hfov 44). Refinement: editor retail vs editor-with-P4-layers water boxes are identical (80.5/80.6 mid, 66.5/66.3 right), so P4 is NOT the cause of the water difference. Real water difference vs game: mid 0.92x (game 99,95.5,100 vs editor 90.8,88.6,93.3); right about 1.0 luma but the editor is greener (B/R 0.88 vs 0.94).
facts.how_to_use: Open: check the FOV mapping (39.20 vs 44) and the blue/haze term near the ground before judging the foliage gap. Sheet: (game left, editor right).

facts.title: P4 layered ground matches the game at the exact pose: quadrant seam and layer assignment are identical, region luma within about 15% on slopes
facts.fact: Same-pose quadrant pair with tracetools-p4.exe and RECOMP_CAM_SET at the exact pose. Program 1 matched; the quadrant seam and the layer assignment are identical between editor and game. Region luma is within about 15% on slopes.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the foreground lighting gap (up to 1.4x) is not explained by layers; it belongs to the lighting or fog terms.

facts.title: The terrain LOD band on a flat map is gone in master; its cause was the micro-fade bug fixed in b8b3937
facts.fact: A band of terrain LOD pop on a flat new map (M03 retail and an UnderCover copy at a player's zoom) no longer appears on master. The cause was the micro-fade bug, fixed in b8b3937.
facts.how_to_use: Open: check a player's own zoom on a second map before calling it closed for all maps.

facts.title: The Mission_05 final water pass (program 00421) mixes tinted refraction with a lit cube reflection, then fog
facts.fact: Decoded from the M05 trace (program 00421): out = fog(lerp(tint x refraction320x240, 2 x cube x light, F x sat(4a))). F = lerp(1.0, 0.769, N.V) (stage constant C0 C4FFFFFF). light = V0 x G.a + G.rgb. V0 = 0.5 x file sun x N.L (0.288 = 0.5 x 0.577, same in all channels). tint = lerp(shallow 137,137,97, deep 100,122,101, T1.a). This is the last of the water's four passes (alpha mask, bump/env reflection, scene-copy refraction, fogged lightmap pass).
facts.how_to_use: Open: compare the editor water to these terms (tint ends, F falloff, V0 sun term) to find the 0.92x mid-water gap. The 4a factor and G values are as decoded; check them at a typical resolution.

facts.title: The editor's Side control writes the unit .Nation property: mission 6 player, 5 enemy, 0 neutral; multiplayer 1 Red, 2 Blue, 0 neutral
facts.fact: Mission inspector Side (Player's side / Enemy / Neutral) and the Units tab 'Placing for' write .Nation = 6, 5 or 0 on the unit or on units placed next. In multiplayer the Placing-for list is Red team / Blue team / Neutral and writes .Nation = 1, 2 or 0 on turrets and soldiers; the MP inspector Side combo (0/1/2) maps to Nation 1/2/0. The trigger action 'Change a unit's side' writes MAActionNation.Nation (6/5/0, default 5).
facts.how_to_use: Open: what apply_unit_side sets beyond Nation (crew and empty flags) is unread. The UX audit wants the mission label 'Player' where the code says Player's side.

facts.title: The Players tab writes MALevelStart.TeamIndex (0 free-for-all, 1 Red, 2 Blue); adding a spawn clones a MALevelStart named Start Point with a new UID
facts.fact: Players tab Free-for-all / Red / Blue write MALevelStart.TeamIndex = 0 / 1 / 2. 'Add spawn' (multiplayer) clones a new MALevelStart named 'Start Point' with a new UID and the chosen TeamIndex, so a side can have several starts. Mission-mode 'Move player start' changes the position of the one mission start (count in mission mode not verified).
facts.how_to_use: Open: the retail count of starts per side is 12 per the wiki while the editor minimum is 6; reconcile in the UX spec.

facts.title: The Map tab game-type checkboxes write one MAMissionTypeGroup flag per game type (ticked = 1, else 0); with none ticked the editor warns on save
facts.fact: The Map tab 'Game types' checkboxes save as a flag on the matching MAMissionTypeGroup per type: 1 if ticked, 0 if not. Team types: Team Destruction, Capture the Flag, Base War, Snatch It, Check It, Team Last Man Standing. Free-for-all types: Destruction, Last Man Standing, Not It, Grinder. If no game type is ticked the editor shows a save warning. The editor writes no default-game-type line (the wiki says a missing GameType means TeamDestruction).
facts.how_to_use: Open: the game-side reader of the per-type flags is not traced; the ini key for game types was not found.

facts.title: 'Give a unit orders' writes an MAAIGroup named [ed] AI Orders per unit, an MAEvent, and an MAPatrol, MADefend, MAFollow or MAAttack order
facts.fact: Order Patrol (default): MAAIGroup '[ed] AI Orders' per unit, then MAEvent (TriggerID = the trigger, Priority 2), then MAPatrol plus MAWaypointGroup (WaypointID = first point) and an MAWaypoint ObjPosition per point; needs 2 or more points. Patrol on an existing map path reparents that MAWaypointGroup under the MAEvent. Defend: MADefend.DefendUID (marker or point), radius write unread. Follow: MAFollow.FollowUID, FollowRadius and FollowDefenseRadius = Radius (default 30). Attack: MAAttack.AttackUID plus AttackPlayer (1 unit, 2 player), AttackSet 0. Labels: Patrol along a path, Defend a point, Follow. Attack.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the [ed] name prefix conflicts with the north star of no parallel [ed] objects; check whether the game needs it or retail uses plain names.

facts.title: The trigger action 'Switch a unit or spawner on or off' writes MAActionAI.ActionEntity = target, AISet = 0 and EnableAI = 1 or 0; it writes no spawner-specific field
facts.fact: The action's 'Switch on' checkbox sets MAActionAI.EnableAI (1 or 0) on the picked unit or spawner (ActionEntity = target, AISet = 0). The editor writes no spawner field. The 'Bring in reinforcements' action is not spawner-based (units are placed hidden and asleep).
facts.how_to_use: Open: whether EnableAI on a MASpawner sets its Enabled bit needs an in-game trace; which editor path creates a MASpawner (generic Add part?) is not traced.

facts.title: The road tool writes MARoad.RoadDefinition, RoadPosition (terrain + 0.15 m) and RoadRotation (yaw) into one Placed Roads MARoadGroup under MATerrain; chaining snaps within 30 m
facts.fact: A palette road piece plus a click writes MARoad.RoadDefinition (the .road path with backslashes, e.g. roads/country/90turn.road), RoadPosition (piece origin; y = terrain height + 0.15 m) and RoadRotation (first float = yaw radians, others 0). All editor-placed pieces go into one MARoadGroup 'Placed Roads' under MATerrain. Chaining joins the next piece to the open end of the previous one (yaw from atan2 difference): 30 m snap radius, 90 m for the last piece. Q/E when snapped picks which end of the new piece joins; unsnapped Q/E turns the heading by 15 degrees. The game reads RoadDefinition at VA 0xD5A19 (documented) and MARoadGroup children in laying order.
facts.how_to_use: Open: says one group per road while the code uses one group for all pieces; check the game does not need separate groups for separate roads.

facts.title: A palette template click clones the retail instance (minus AI, path, objective, event and kill-reference children) under Placed Objects; categories and search aliases only filter the list
facts.fact: Picking a palette template and clicking clones the retail instance into 'Placed Objects' with its AI, path, objective, event and kill-reference children stripped (full property list not checked). Palette categories (for example Roads and pavement) and the search aliases (pavement, intersection and road-piece terms; country roads sorted first) write nothing to the map; they only filter and sort the list.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the UX audit proposes a Roads category and plain piece names; the code still says Roads and pavement.

facts.title: The editor's object list (Everything in this map) is display only: objects are grouped by kind, and helpers (triggers, AI paths, markers, lights, cameras, other logic) are listed last
facts.fact: The section 'Everything in this map' lists every placed object except parts under a root, with a Find box and a count 'N things (M helpers)'. Groups are headed 'Kind (count)', sorted with Water first; groups of 8 or fewer open by default and the list caps at 400 rows. Helpers go last under 'Helpers (not shown in the game)': Trigger areas, AI paths (waypoints), Markers (MADummyObj), Lights (MAPointLight), Cameras and camera paths (MAFreeCamera, MACinema), Other logic (other non-model classes). Roads, water, spawns, crates, effects and flags are drawn by the game and are not helpers. Listing and grouping write nothing to the map file.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the 'Show helpers' toggles (key H, one checkbox per group) hide the drawing only; the list still shows helper rows when a group is off.

facts.title: In the object list a row click selects (Ctrl adds), double-click frames the object, and Rename (F2) writes the object's Description
facts.fact: Row click selects an object (Ctrl adds to the selection); double-click or 'Show on the map' frames it; neither writes to the map. The right-click menu offers Show on the map, Rename (F2), Duplicate (Ctrl+D) and Delete (Del). Rename writes the Description property when committed; Duplicate and Delete change the map as ordinary edits.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the duplicate and delete handlers were not read. The UX audit R7 wants eye, lock and side-colour toggles on rows; none were found.

facts.title: The editor's side ring (two circles under each unit, hidden by H) is view only: Nation 5 red, 6 blue in missions; 1 red, 2 blue in multiplayer; anything else grey
facts.fact: Two concentric 32-segment circles are drawn on the terrain under each MECH, TANK, VEHICLE, FLYER, TURRET and PERSON that has a Nation field. Radius is max(2, 0.6 x footprint), at least 2.5 x marker scale. Mission colours: Nation 5 (Enemy) red (255,90,90), 6 (Player's side) blue (110,160,255), other grey (200,200,200). Multiplayer: 1 (Red team) red, 2 (Blue team) blue, other grey. The object list shows the same colour as a dot before each unit row. The Nation value is saved (set_nation writes it); the ring and the dot are not saved. The ring answers the audit item that sides were not visible.
facts.how_to_use: Open: there is no text label for the ring or a separate toggle other than the helpers key H.

facts.title: Retail MAAIGroup objects are named plain 'AI Orders' (events 'AI Event', numeric suffix for duplicates); no retail name has an [ed] prefix
facts.fact: A dump of every MAAIGroup in 19 mission files plus SPDemoMission found 207 instances. Their name is stored in the Description key 1487300E (editor label Name). Retail uses plain names: 'AI Orders' (118 instances, e.g. Mission_01b), 'AI Orders_00000', 'AI Orders_00001'; events are 'AI Event', 'AI Event_00000'. Duplicates get numeric suffixes. No retail name has an [ed] prefix. No code was found that looks up an MAAIGroup, MAEvent or MAPatrol by name; the catalog describes the name as the label shown in the editor object list. The editor writes the name '[ed] AI Orders'.
facts.how_to_use: Recommendation: write the plain name AI Orders (and AI Event) for one-to-one retail parity. Open: whether any generic lookup compares the Description CRC 1487300E at runtime is unchecked in the recompiled code.

facts.title: The Starts hidden checkbox (commit 50600b8) writes a MATriggerTimer named Hidden at start and a child MAActionShow (ActionEntity = unit, Enable = 0)
facts.fact: In the Units inspector, for MAMech, MATank, MAVehicle, MAFlyer, MATurret and MAPerson, ticking 'Starts hidden' reuses or creates a MATriggerTimer 'Hidden at start' and adds a child MAActionShow 'Hide <unit>' with ActionEntity = the unit's uid and Enable = 0. The timer duration is not set by the commit (it relies on the add_trigger_object default). Unticking pushes undo 'starts hidden' and removes every hide action pointing at the unit; the timer stays. The box shows ticked when any MAActionShow with Enable 0 hangs off a MATriggerTimer with TrgTimerDurationSeconds <= 0.01 and targets the unit, so hand-made hiders count too. Ticking also turns on View > Objects the mission shows later so the unit stays visible while editing. The game side follows the retail Mission_05 pattern (a 0-second start timer hides the unit; a later trigger with MAActionShow Enable 1 shows it); that is documented, not runtime-tested here.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the default TrgTimerDurationSeconds that add_trigger_object gives a new MATriggerTimer (if not 0 the tick is never detected); whether Enable 1 from a later trigger reveals the unit without a separate AI enable.

facts.title: The Starting orders block (commit 05b294d) reads a unit's MAAIGroup/MAEvent/behaviour children; Give this unit orders writes a timer, MAAIGroup, MAEvent and a patrol or attack behaviour plus a path
facts.fact: In the mission Properties panel, non-multiplayer units with Nation != 0 of class MAMech, MATank, MAVehicle, MAFlyer, MATurret or MAPerson get a 'Starting orders' block that lists each order in plain words with an Edit button and 'Give this unit orders.'. It reads the unit's MAAIGroup children, their MAEvent children, the behaviour child (MAPatrol path length, MADefend.DefendUID, MAFollow.FollowUID, MAAttack AttackPlayer/AttackUID) and the trigger's MATriggerTimer duration for 'when the mission starts'. 'Give this unit orders' writes a MATriggerTimer 'Orders: <unit>', an MAAIGroup under the unit if none exists, an MAEvent (Description 'AI Event', then 'AI Event_00000', TriggerID, Priority 2), a behaviour child (MAPatrol, or MAAttack for turrets) and an add_ai_path named '<unit> - patrol path' reparented under the event; then the editor enters point-placing mode. The event names are plain AI Event, matching retail.
facts.how_to_use: Open: which property values set_order_kind writes (the diff was truncated).

facts.title: The Player Spawner (commit 05b294d) is only a lookup: the editor treats the MALevelStart whose description is exactly Player Spawner as the player start, else the first MALevelStart
facts.fact: player_start_uid returns the MALevelStart whose description is exactly 'Player Spawner', else the first MALevelStart. It is used by 'Move player start', by MAFollow and MAAttack player targets, and for the compiled player reference. The commit creates and names no object. The commit's claim that the game uses the MALevelStart named Player Spawner is not supported by the diff: wiki facts say MAFollow.FollowUID and MAAttack.AttackUID reference the player's MALevelStart, but none say the game reads a description string.
facts.how_to_use: Open: does the game read MALevelStart.Description, or only class and UID references? Low confidence that the name matters.

facts.title: The multiplayer Player starts block (commit e71e2a8) arms Place Spawn per side and counts MALevelStart.TeamIndex; fewer than 6 per ticked team type triggers an orange warning
facts.fact: The Units tab for multiplayer maps shows a 'Player starts' block with Red, Blue and Free-for-all buttons, each with a count of MALevelStart.TeamIndex 1, 2 and 0. Clicking arms Tool:PlaceSpawn with the team; placing calls ScenarioIO:add_spawn, which clones a MALevelStart with TeamIndex 0/1/2, Description 'Start Point', y = terrain + 2, heading in StartOrientation, in the 'Red/Blue/Spawn Points' group under 'Team Spawns' or 'FFA Spawns'. Orange text warns when a ticked team type has fewer than 6 Red or Blue starts, or a ticked free-for-all type has fewer than 6 FFA starts; a hint says real maps have about 12 a side (text only). Missions show only 'Move player start' (moves the first MALevelStart, or adds a team-0 start if none exists). The commit adds no remove control; per-side counts are advisory only.
facts.how_to_use: Open: which start the game picks for a given player or bot and whether it honours TeamIndex; whether the 12-a-side figure is right for retail (the wiki says 12).

facts.title: Retail patrols use MAAIGroup > MAEvent (Priority mostly 2) > MAPatrol with a sibling MAWaypointGroup; waypoint speeds are 0, 11, 15, 60 or 100; patrolling tanks on M01b start with AI off
facts.fact: Retail field check by inspect_wdf on M08, M01b, M03 and M05: the layout MAAIGroup > MAEvent (TriggerID, Priority) > MAPatrol, with the MAWaypointGroup as its sibling, is the same as the editor's. MAEvent Priority is mostly 2 (M01b 25 events, M03 24 events). WaypointSpeed on retail patrol paths is 0, 11, 15, 60 or 100 (M03 uses 0), so 0 is a legal retail value. StayOnPath is 0 or 1; TraverseType is 1 everywhere. Retail patrolling tanks on M01b (9 MATank) start with m_bAIEnabled 0 and are started by Logic or Radius triggers; people have AI 1. The editor's patrol data matches this layout field by field, so no field-level cause was found for a Partisan that does not drive.
facts.how_to_use: Open: whether MAPatrol needs the unit's AI on, whether waypoint speed 0 means the unit's own speed, and whether engagement overrides patrol. Suggested proof: an M01b-style MATank or a mech instead of the Partisan, with a 5-second timer.

facts.title: An AI order (MAEvent + MAPatrol) on a unit with m_bAIEnabled 0 does nothing; the unit must be woken with MAActionAI EnableAI 1 (game run)
facts.fact: Wiki fact dormant-units-need-startup-hide (verified in game) shows placed units saved with m_bAIEnabled 0 stand with their AI asleep until a trigger runs MAActionShow Enable 1 and MAActionAI EnableAI 1; retail patrolling tanks on M01b have m_bAIEnabled 0 and are started by Logic or Radius triggers. So a patrol needs the unit's AI on, which the editor's Give orders does not currently set (inferred, not tested). Structure: unit > MAAIGroup > MAEvent (TriggerID, Priority) > MAPatrol with the MAWaypointGroup as sibling, same as retail. Not found in code: the dispatcher reading TriggerID and Priority, the meaning of TriggerID 0, and the meaning of WaypointSpeed 0 (float at MAWaypointGroup +0x68, no consumer found). Editor WaypointID = first MAWaypoint uid, retail cinema groups use the last (unresolved). UPDATE: confirmed. An AI order on a unit with m_bAIEnabled 0 does nothing; the unit must be woken by MAActionAI EnableAI 1 (ActionEntity = the unit). Retail M01b patrolling MATanks are all AI-off and are woken by their Logic triggers' 'Entity Enable' actions. The editor now adds a 'Wake <unit>' action with every order.
facts.how_to_use: Remaining open: what WaypointSpeed 0 means, what TriggerID 0 means at runtime (common in retail: 12 of 22 missions), whether a hostile target suspends a patrol, and key 2A68614F (0 on every retail patrol). Resolved: WaypointID = first waypoint of the group matches retail (9 of 9).

facts.title: Unit orders (commit 4337abb) also add a Wake <unit> action: MAActionAI with ActionEntity = the unit and EnableAI = 1, under the trigger that starts the order
facts.fact: In add_order the editor adds an MAActionAI labelled 'Wake <unit description>' with ActionEntity = the unit UID and EnableAI = 1, parented to the order's trigger. facts.title: 'Make it reinforcements.' (commit 8e11eb5, merged in 6f95ef9) writes a NULL holder > MASpawner (Enabled 0, TriggerEnableID, 1 / 1) > the unit; it creates no trigger
facts.fact: Button 'Make it reinforcements.' with fields 'Arrives when' (trigger), 'How many', 'At once', 'Seconds between'. It writes a NULL holder (template 32093, tmpdev NULL.NODE, invisible, Description 'Reinforcements: <unit>') and an MASpawner child: Enabled 0, TriggerEnableID = the chosen trigger UID (0 until chosen), MaxSpawners 1, MaxActiveSpawners 1, SpawnRate 0, SpawnDelay 0; StartDisabled is not written. The unit is reparented under the spawner. No trigger is created. In game (wiki reinforcements-spawner-pattern, documented): 157 of 167 campaign spawners are Enabled 0 with TriggerEnableID = a trigger UID. A spawn needs the Enabled bit, NumSpawned < MaxSpawners, NumActive < MaxActiveSpawners and time past NextSpawnTime; SpawnRate is the gap (spawner-runtime-offsets, code-confirmed). facts.title: MARoad.RoadPosition is the road piece's start end (its origin); turning a selected piece about its footprint middle (commit 6151cba) rewrites RoadPosition so the middle stays fixed

The only extra write is RoadPosition: c + off - R(theta) x off, where off is the half-length along the piece's -Z; Y is unchanged and the heading changes on the root.

facts.title: Roof and bridge placing (commit 078631d, G10) moves the placing ghost and the click to the top of a model, so a placed prop takes the roof's Y; only the position changes
facts.fact: While placing a prop (not a road, not with Alt), cursor_object_top casts the cursor ray against the top plane of unrotated model boxes at least 1 m above terrain. If the ray enters that top before the ground, the ghost and the click use that point: X and Z from the hit and Y = the roof top. No new property is written; unit side rings are drawn flat at their feet (render only). It uses model boxes, not triangles, and skips pitched or rolled models.

facts.title: Retail patrols: the MAWaypointGroup (sibling of MAPatrol under the MAEvent) has WaypointID = its FIRST waypoint; MAEvent.TriggerID is a trigger uid and 0 is common; speed 0 sits beside non-zero speeds
facts.fact: Retail dump (inspect_wdf on mission_01b and mission_03): MAPatrol itself has no WaypointID; the sibling MAWaypointGroup under the same MAEvent has WaypointID = the FIRST waypoint of its child-sibling chain in 9 of 9 event groups (e.g. 01b group 132506 -> 132504, first of [132504,132505]; 03 group 124214 -> 124215). This matches the editor's convention. MAEvent.TriggerID is the uid of a trigger (MATriggerLogic, Radius, Destroyed, Timer or CuboidalVolume). TriggerID 0 appears in 12 of 22 missions; mission_04 has 24 of 34 events at 0. In mission_01b event 132507 points to MATriggerRadius 130888, which has a child MAActionAI 'Entity Enable'; event 132502 points to MATriggerLogic 132615 with no Entity Enable, so the start trigger is the TriggerID trigger only when it carries the Entity Enable action (MEDIUM, one pair). Patrol-event groups in 01b have speeds 11, 15, 40 (no 0); in 03 all 6 are 0.0; unit-owned groups mix 0 and non-zero for the same class (03 MATank 0.0 x11 vs 4.0 x1), which does not prove 0 means unit default (LOW). An unnamed key 2A68614F is 0 on every retail patrol. COUNT CAVEAT: the catalog counts TriggerID 0 in 47 of 360 retail events (about 13 percent); the researcher's figures '12 of 22 missions' (missions with at least one) and 'Mission_04 24 of 34 events' come from a separate dump and were not cross-checked, so treat 'common' as: present in many missions, a minority of all events.
facts.how_to_use: Open: what key 2A68614F is and whether the editor writes it; what speed 0 does at runtime. Command: python inspect_wdf.py mission_01b --output <file> in the bringup folder.

facts.title: Code search found no direct runtime reader of MAWaypointGroup.WaypointSpeed, MAEvent.TriggerID or MASpawner.TriggerEnableID (dead ends recorded; the meaning of 0 stays open)
facts.fact: WaypointSpeed (key 4B22EAB8, float at MAWaypointGroup +0x68, catalog offset 136): sub_0012ED73 (read) and sub_0012EAF2 (write) are vtable 0x46FD64 slots 1 and 0, the generic property get and set handlers, with no direct call sites; so the value is reached through the property system and no mover reader was isolated. No 'speed == 0 means default' fallback was found in the patrol or traverse functions. MASpawner.TriggerEnableID (key 0x9758CB1A, +0x80 uint): only reflective and serializer code touches it (sub_0013270D at 0x132E6B read, sub_00132C92 formats and writes, sub_00133DB2 copies); the spawner tick sub_0013321F does not read it, and the code that flips Enabled when the trigger fires was not found. MAEvent.TriggerID (key 0xF3773A85): no runtime reader located; the catalog says 'Starts when' and counts 0 in 47 of 360 retail events. The MAEvent functions sub_000D44AE to sub_000D46B1 in recomp_0021.c were listed but not checked.

facts.title: How deep retail water is where the type map says wade (8) or deep (16): shallow cells are about 0.3-2 m under the surface (flat MP lakes 2.9-4.4 m), deep cells 2-8 m
facts.fact: Measured on all 15 campaign worlds and 15 multiplayer worlds with MAWater planes: for every type-map cell with bit 8 / 16 / 32 inside a plane, depth = plane CorporalPos.y minus the bilinear terrain height (8-bit height field, TerrainMinHeight.MaxHeight). SHALLOW (8): median 0.3-1.2 m and 90th percentile <=1.6 m on nearly every map: Bogged Down swamp median 0.9 / p90 1.2 / max 1.7; Mission_07 1.0 / 1.3 (max 5.0); New River City 1.2 / 1.6 (max 2.3); Mission_06a 0.3 / 1.1; Mission_14 0.7 / 1.4 (max 4.6); Mission_11a 0.8 / 2.5 (max 4.0). Flat-bottomed MP lakes are deeper but uniform: No Man's Land 2.9 m, Troubled Waters 4.4 m. DEEP (16, campaign only): Mission_01b night harbour 8.1 m, Mission_02 median 5.9 (p10 2.9), Cinema_1_3 5.9, Mission_11a median 4.7 (p90 6.8), Mission_14 median 2.2 (p90 4.1), Mission_06a 1.9. WATERWAY (32): median 0.6-1.2 m, p90 <=1.4 on most worlds. So retail never has an 8-marked wading cell deeper than about 4.4 m (typical <2 m) and puts bit 16 only where the water is deeper than about 2-3 m. The game does not read a depth to decide wading: gameplay water is the type-map bit plus the MAEnvironment per-type values (Speed / Damage / Cooling / 'Mech may enter' / Pilot in - shallow, deep, waterway). The editor's default dig makes a 200x120 lake ~8 m deep at the middle with every cell below the surface marked 8 (water_ux.cpp dig_water_basin: depth = min(pond_depth_ 8, max(1, 0.3 x shorter half side))), 2-4x the deepest retail shallow water; in game the on-foot pilot walks out of the start, sinks fully under the surface and the camera sits at the waterline.
facts.how_to_use: Use for the c3 water owner: a wadable lake should dig 1-2 m (retail median 0.9-1.2 m, p90 <=1.6; 2.9-4.4 m exists only as flat MP lakes) or be warned/capped. Visibility trade-off: the editor comment says shallow water is faint in the game (thickness alpha ~ vertical depth/4, medium, see water-thickness-alpha-samples), which is why pond_depth_ starts at 8. Open: no game code was found that drowns, slows or pushes out a pilot below the surface (the pilot follows the terrain bed; no swim state found); what bit 16 does for an on-foot pilot (Pilot in - deep water: 1.0 x51, 100.0 x11, 0.0 x3, 10.0 x1 in the catalog, meaning unconfirmed) is untested; planes overlapping a larger plane (OverFalls pool 7.5 m) and a few negative depths come from cells outside the assumed plane extent (model size from the template name 1000/500/250).

facts.title: Pickups palette (G-c, d793a3a): weapon upgrades first, then the bomb, armour repairs by tonnage, the data core last; plain names such as 'Armor repair (15T)'. It changes the palette label and order only, not the placed object

facts.title: Sides & Units > Player starts shows one line per ticked game type: green 'Ready: <type>' or amber 'Needs work: <type>'; hover lists what is missing. It is the Check scenario list filtered to that type (c2918fd)
facts.fact: For every ticked game type (s.types), the line takes the Check scenario errors (level 2) whose text starts with the type's label and shows them as the tooltip; no such error = Ready. validate runs at most twice a second. The checks come from validate in scenario.cpp, per ticked type, counting only objects active in that type (inside MAMissionTypeGroups whose flag for the type is non-zero): team types (Team Destruction, Capture the Flag, Base War, Snatch It, Check It, Team Last Man Standing) need >= 6 MALevelStart with TeamIndex 1 (Red) and >= 6 with TeamIndex 2 (Blue); free-for-all types (Destruction, Last Man Standing, Not It, Grinder) need >= 6 with TeamIndex 0; extra objects per type (mode_requirements): CTF needs an MAFlagCTF (and one for each team: description containing red / blue), Snatch It needs MASnatchItBase and MASnatchItDataCore, Base War needs MAObjectiveType and objectives 0 (Red power plant) and 1 (Blue); spacing warnings (level 1, not part of Ready): two spawns within 3 m, enemy-team spawns within 60 m. It replaces the old fixed text 'Team game types need at least 6 Red and 6 Blue starts'.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the 6 per side minimum is the editor's rule (retail maps have about 12); the game-side parse of the game-type flags is still unread.

facts.title: A unit placed from the palette for a side in a mission now gets m_bAIEnabled 1 (717af5f); before, it kept the template's AI-off and stood inert. Not done in multiplayer or for side-less placements
facts.fact: place_object (app_tools.cpp) calls apply_unit_side, then, when the document is a mission (not multiplayer), place_side_ is not 0 and the unit has m_bAIEnabled, sets m_bAIEnabled 1. Reason: retail unit templates are mostly saved AI-off (asleep until a trigger wakes them, e.g. M01b tanks), so an enemy placed in a mission stood still while the inspector said it 'fights whatever comes close'. Game run: enemy Manticore from a palette click with no orders moves, aims and fires missiles at the player (see ai-on-hostile-unit-with-no-ai-group-engages-the-player-by-itself-runtime-observed). The unit's Starting orders summary now says 'None, and its AI is off: it stays still and does not fight. Tick AI enabled below, or give it orders (they switch its AI on)' for AI-off units (orders add a Wake action, see the wake-action fact).

facts.title: Check scenario warns 'its patrol route has N point(s), so it will not move' for a MAPatrol whose MAWaypointGroup has fewer than 2 MAWaypoints; routes with no group at all are left alone
facts.fact: validate walks every MAPatrol, finds the event's waypoint group (order_path) and counts the MAWaypoint children; if the group exists and has <2, it adds a level-1 warning naming the unit, linking to it. A patrol with no group is skipped because retail Mission_01b has such patrols (e.g. 'tank at wall (was raptor)'), so a fresh M01b copy shows no false warnings. Fix text: open the unit's orders on the Triggers tab and press Draw on map (2 or more points). Why 2: a 1-point route has nowhere to go; with TraverseType 1 a 2-point route is driven once, with 2 it loops (see the TraverseType fact).
facts.how_to_use: Open: what retail does with its empty-group patrols (they are probably AI-off tanks woken by Entity Enable and given routes elsewhere).

facts.title: Place water + Dig a basin now digs about 1.4 m (kWadeDepth) so an on-foot pilot wades through (game-proven g3); the 'Deep (only 'Mechs can wade)' tick restores up to 8 m. This follows the retail depth measurement

The cap was proven on g3: the pilot wades. The type-map write is unchanged: every playable cell below the surface gets value 8. Ticking Deep keeps 'Mechs able to walk through; the pilot goes under.

facts.title: The type-map water ground (value 8) now follows each water object: moving, resizing, re-levelling or deleting a water returns the cells it no longer covers to plain ground and marks the new footprint (27ff6ab)
facts.fact: track_water_ground runs every frame: it keeps each MAWater's last footprint (centre, width, length, heading, oval) in water_feet_; when one changes or disappears, the type-map cells (value 8) of the old footprint that the water no longer covers are cleared to 0 and the new footprint is marked with mark_water_ground (cells whose ground lies below the surface). Before, a moved or deleted water left an invisible wading area behind. Skipped on read-only documents and maps without a type map.

facts.title: An editor 'Attack a unit' order with the class-default 'Give up after' 3 s (MAAttack AttackTimeout, key FCFD971B) makes the unit fire ONE volley and stop; 9999 keeps the fight going. New editor Attack orders write 9999 ('Keep attacking until the target is gone')

The same map with AttackTimeout 9999 -> several volleys, hits, the enemy fires back, both leave the view by ~66 s. Catalog (retail dump of 89 MAAttack behaviours): AttackTimeout float at MAAttack serializer +96 = runtime object +0x80 (loader sub_000D49C6, write sub_000D48C0), class default 3.0, retail values 3.0 x47, 6.0 x11, 9999 x8, up to 99999 (11 distinct); label 'Give up after', tooltip '[text omitted]'. Editor: new Attack orders write AttackTimeout 9999; the Orders view shows the checkbox 'Keep attacking until the target is gone' (off writes 3 and shows 'Stop attacking after (s)', a float field on the same key). Attack-the-player (AttackPlayer 2) by an ALLY (nation 6) fired one shot at the start, no damage seen (PARTIAL, LOW).

UPDATE: the runtime reader is sub_001854C5 (see attack-order-target-chooser-sub-001854c5.); older note: the per-frame reader was not found (the load site sub_000D4941 at recomp_0022.c:309 reads +0x60 as a float and the setter sub_000D482C stores it; the copy function at 0xD4A32 does NOT copy it; the catalog code.offset 128 is wrong, +0x60 = 96 matches its own evidence text; the MAAttack vtable 0x466618 has no tick, so the runtime owner is probably an MABehavior/AI-group update); whether it counts from the order start or each shot and what the unit does on expiry is only known from the game run (stops after one volley); the editor's 'Keep attacking' default differs from retail's modal value 3 s on purpose.

facts.title: Defend and Follow orders written by the editor are game-proven: a MADefend unit drives to its DefendUID marker and holds; a MAFollow ally re-joins the player after the player moves away

facts.fact: Game (wiki maspawner-spawn-rules + spawner-runtime-offsets, code-confirmed): the spawner tick sub_0013321F (recomp) returns without spawning unless the Enabled flag (+0x78 bit 0x01) is set and bit 0x10 is clear, NumSpawned (+0x98) < MaxSpawners (+0x7C) unless MaxSpawners is 0, NumActive (+0x9C) < MaxActiveSpawners (+0x90) unless that is 0, and the clock is past NextSpawnTime; a spawn increments NumSpawned and NumActive and sets NextSpawnTime = now + SpawnRate (the first spawn waits SpawnDelay). facts.title: The game reads MAAttack AttackTimeout in sub_001854C5 (a 'choose target' helper): with AttackPlayer 1 the unit sticks to its current target until elapsed time since a per-unit stamp exceeds AttackTimeout, then takes the order's target; AttackPlayer 0 always takes the order's target, AttackPlayer 2 (the player) switches when the player is farther than a range
facts.fact: recomp_0040.c:17651-17800 sub_001854C5 (edi = the AI unit; code-confirmed incl. the x87 order: clock - [unit+0x100] is compared with the timeout, ja = elapsed > timeout). Steps: the unit's current order event is [unit+0x1A8], its behaviour [event+0x7C]; the behaviour's class id [beh+0x28] must equal MEM32(0x4EAF1C) (MAAttack, else the helper just returns the current target [unit+0xB4]); unit+0xF0 = the behaviour's +0x2C, the order's target is resolved by sub_001855E7(unit, behaviour) (runtime AttackUID at beh+0x78, AttackSet +0x7C), validated by sub_000B3C50 and stored to unit+0xF4. If the unit has NO current target ([unit+0xB4] == 0) or AttackPlayer (beh+0x84) == 0 the order's target is returned at once. AttackPlayer 1 ('attack a unit'): elapsed = the live clock (double at 0x4E2440) minus the float stamp [unit+0x100]; if elapsed > AttackTimeout (beh+0x80) it returns the order's target, else it keeps the current target. AttackPlayer 2 ('attack the player'): no timeout test; it takes the distance between two positions (the current target and the order's target) and returns the CURRENT target if the squared distance is below [[unit+0x20]+0x200] squared (a range read from the unit's class data), otherwise the ORDER's target. Runtime object offsets are the serializer offsets + 0x20 (the constructor sub_000D476C stores the vtable at obj+0x20): AttackUID +0x78, AttackSet +0x7C, AttackTimeout +0x80, AttackPlayer +0x84. Callers store the result into unit+0xB4 after a unit vtable +0x20 call (nine sites: recomp_0046.c:15293, 27730, 27952, 29373; recomp_0047.c:7841, 8068, 30150; plus 0x1BACF6 x2).
facts.how_to_use: Meaning for authors: AttackTimeout is NOT a countdown that ends the order. It is how long the unit may go without a fresh 'event' stamp before it re-targets the ordered unit; the stamp [unit+0x100] is written by sub_0018519F (shifts +0xF8/+0x100 history, stores the clock; probably last hit or last engagement - inferred). A large value (9999) keeps whatever the unit is fighting; 3 s snaps back to the ordered target quickly. Open: callers of sub_0018519F (stamp meaning) and what happens when the returned target equals the current one; AttackPlayer 0 is used by 2 of 89 retail attacks, 1 by 42, 2 by 45.

facts.title: Mission variables: the game has 30 (0.29, one byte each) shared by objective slots (ob<i>var0), MAActionMissionVariableSet actions and trigger/camera MissionVariable gates; retail MARoot fills UNUSED objective slots with var 0, so 'slot index = variable' only holds for new maps
facts.fact: Mission_14 slot 10 and Mission_15 slot 7 carry ob%dvar0 = 0 as filler for an unused slot (no ObjectiveItemDesc), and Mission_01b's retail triggers (e.g. 'TT - delay post barge dest', 'TD - jack mech (now dest tanks)') set variable 16, which is exactly the index a 17th objective would take, so the new objective finished at once. claim_objective_var now treats var 0 on an empty slot as unclaimed, then marks as used every number set by an MAActionMissionVariableSet (MissionVariableSet), every numeric trigger/camera MissionVariable gate and every other slot's ob<j>var<n>, and picks the slot index if free, else the first free number from 1.29, with 0 last (0 is settable but never gates a trigger). fmt_test --all-maps checks every mission.

facts.title: Terrain heights are stored as 8 bits between the map's min_h and max_h (editor default -20.100 m); Raise/Lower/Plateau strokes clamp to that range, and the editor now says so (Advanced > Height range)
facts.fact: terrain.h: 'Writes heights (quantized to 8 bits between min_h and max_h) and the range into MATerrain'; default min_h -20, max_h 100 (core/terrain.h:20, scenario.h:99). The Raise/Lower status in the editor (app.cpp ~3398) reports the whole stroke's actual change after the clamp (stroke_change_ = |h - h_in|) , when the ground is already at the map's highest/lowest height, says it cannot go higher/lower and points to Advanced > Height range. The step size of the 8-bit quantisation is (max_h - min_h)/255, about 0.47 m at the default range.
facts.how_to_use: Use: the ceiling that stops a raise is the map's own max_h, not a game constant; widening the range coarsens the height step. Display-only status text otherwise (no new game value).

facts.fact: HUD health full (the mech was not hurt). Template data: Env_WideBridge02 MABuilding Indestructible 0, MAMaxHitPoints 1800, MinDamThres 2, ReceivesCollisionDamage 1, DestroyedBuilding 117552 = Env_Widebridge02_CS (MACorporealDestroyed, IsCollidable 0, CausesCollisionDamage 1, DamageAmount 250, DamageTimer 4, models with cut_section / env_widebridge_sectionone/two meshes). Retail Mission_03 treats the bridges as a destroy objective ('Bridges' set + MATriggerDestroyed 'Player Did It', MAActionRemoveEntity 'Remove Bridge', enemy 'Bridge Crosser' units cross them). NOT PROVEN: no game log line was read, the second candidate (the deck sat 0.7-0.9 m BELOW the plateau the mech walked in , retail has it 0.27 above) is not excluded. Discriminating tests: set Indestructible=1 on the three pieces and retry; or place the chain with the road surface 0.27 m above the plateau; or play the same map with the pieces' ReceivesCollisionDamage 0. RESULT: FAIL old pieces h 41.0 (road 0.9 m below plateau), Indestructible 0: deck collapses under the mech (debris, mech ends under the deck). FAIL old pieces road 0.7 m below plateau with Indestructible=1 set by --set-prop. PASS old pieces raised to h 42.15 (road 0.27 m above plateau, as retail M03), Indestructible 1: whole chain crossed, no debris. PASS pit test with deck at retail ground height, Indestructible 0. PASS fresh palette-placed pieces (editor 6c65b92: Indestructible 1 and the template's set links dropped) at h 41.0 = road 0.9 m below the plateau: crossed, only dust/chips.
